data.name: Iceland

sources.label: Freedom House: country electoral and political indicators, 2026 edition

legitimacy.summary:
Our assessment: Iceland has broadly credible and competitive national electoral institutions. The latest country indicators support meaningful voter choice, sound electoral rules and an opposition able to contest governing power. This is not a guarantee that every contest is flawless, nor a judgement about the popularity of any party.

Evidence baseline: Freedom in the World 2026, covering conditions in 2025. Our review date is not the date of an observer verdict on a later ballot; subsequent contests may require a separate assessment.

data.coverageNote: Selected records only. Earlier elections and additional result detail are still being added.

data.notes: The early election renewed all 63 seats. Six parties won representation. Vote totals and shares are intentionally blank pending confirmation against Statistics Iceland.
data.title: Althing

sources.label: IPU Parline: Iceland 30 November 2024 election, sourced to parliament

data.summary: The Social Democratic Alliance won 15 of 63 seats, followed by the Independence Party with 14.
data.voteBasis: Seats by party from the Inter-Parliamentary Union, sourced to Iceland's parliament. Party vote totals and shares have not yet been entered.
data.government: Social Democratic Alliance, Reform and People's Party formed a 36-seat coalition.
